transcript.text: My Dyson V10 Absolute (SV12) won't run at all now. On the battery display there's a red light flashing when I press the trigger, then nothing. It was charging overnight. Do I need a new battery or is the whole thing dead?

A flashing red light when pressing the trigger usually means the vacuum’s safety system has cut power. This is most often due to a blocked filter or airway triggering protection, rather than the whole unit being dead. However, if the battery isn't holding charge properly, it can also show this behaviour. To narrow this down: when you put the vacuum on charge, does the light on the charger (or dock) stay solid green/blue, or does it flash red/amber?
[Helpful to see: image "Poor suction — what to check first" — A vacuum that pulses or cuts out after running is usually a full bin, a dirty filter or a blockage starving the airflow — check and clear those before suspecting battery, charger or motor. Switch off and unplug first. Typical layout — your model may differ.]

The charger light is on and the blue lights come up on the vacuum while it charges, but it sometimes then shows the flashing red too. The filter was washed last month and the bin is empty, so I don't think it's a blockage. The red light is definitely flashing, about once a second.

[Heading: Likely battery protection or cell failure]
Switch it off and unplug it (or take the battery off) first. The flashing red light is a safety cut-out. Please do this quick check: remove both filters (pre-motor and HEPA), ensure they are completely dry inside, and look through the wand to make sure nothing is blocking it. Then try running the vacuum on 'Normal' mode only for a few seconds. If it runs normally now, it was likely just a damp filter or blockage. If it still flashes red immediately even with clean/dry filters and no blockages, the battery is likely failing and needs replacing.

I took the filters out and looked through the wand. The filters are clean and dry (washed last month) and there's no blockage. It still just flashes red and the motor won't start on any mode. The battery isn't swollen, hot or smelly. It's the original battery, about 4.5 years old, and the runtime had dropped to about 8 minutes before it stopped. Is it a new battery then?

[Heading: Worn battery]
It is the battery. A flashing red light when you press the trigger indicates the vacuum’s safety system has cut power because it detects a fault with the battery voltage or communication. Given that your original battery is 4.5 years old and the runtime had already dropped to just 8 minutes before this happened, it has reached the end of its life. The good news is that the rest of the vacuum (the motor and electronics) is likely fine; Dyson vacuums are designed so that a failing battery triggers a safety cut-out rather than damaging the main unit. You will need to replace the battery pack. Since it is an original part from 4.5 years ago, I recommend buying a new genuine or high-quality compatible battery for your V10 model. Once you have the new battery, install it and try running the vacuum on 'Normal' mode first (avoid 'Max/Boost' mode initially to ensure it holds charge). If it runs normally, the issue is resolved. If you ever need help finding a replacement or have questions about installation, feel free to ask.
